messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–75 mph on highways, 25–45 mph in residential areas.
• “No speed limit” zones exist on some rural roads. | Speed limits are posted; exceeding them can lead to fines and points. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Stop signs: stop, yield to pedestrians, then proceed. | Failure to yield can lead to points and fines. | | **School Bus** | • Must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• No passing in either direction. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and 2 points. | | **Headlights** | • Must be used from sunset to sunrise, and during inclement weather. | Failure to use headlights can lead to a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid license and insurance. | Unregistered vehicles can be towed and fined. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points vary by offense (e.g., DUI = 4 points). | Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Speed cameras and red‑light cameras are used in many cities. | Violations are mailed to the registered owner. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or stop sign.
• Pay‑and‑display or meter required in many urban areas. | Parking violations can result in fines and towing. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18.
• Commercial vehicles: must have a valid commercial driver’s license (CDL). | Failure to comply can lead to fines and license suspension. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and updates. - **Local County Ordinances**: May have additional rules (e.g., speed limits, parking restrictions). ### Quick Resources - **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – downloadable PDF. - **Texas.gov – Driver’s License & Vehicle Registration** – online portal. - **Texas A&M Transportation Institute** – research and statistics. --- **Tip:** If you’re planning to drive in Texas, it’s a good idea to review the most recent Texas Transportation Code and check local county ordinances for any specific rules that might differ from state law.
